answer.value: Yes: Ferrowind should stop charging a full seat for every user. Move off pure per-seat pricing to usage-based pricing or a hybrid that charges builders/editors (or a platform fee) and makes view-only or occasional users free or near free.
answer.derivation: Of 11 losses in the deal notes, 7 were on seat price and only 3 on missing features (Quarrydown reclassified from price to feature), plus 1 in-house build. All 7 seat-price losses were about paying a seat for occasional or view-only users, which Ferrowind's pricing requires (every named user including viewers needs a seat). Six went to competitors that do not charge every user a seat: Tallowbeam (now usage-based since August 2026), Obsidra (credits, unlimited users) and Brisklane (free viewers). The seventh went to Sorrelgate, whose platform fee includes 5 seats with cheaper extra seats. The two pure per-seat competitors, Quillmark and Kettleridge, only won on features. The market has moved the same way: 2 of 6 competitors are usage-based, 1 charges editors only, 1 is a hybrid platform fee.
answer.counts_if: Recommends moving away from charging every user a seat (full usage pricing or a hybrid with free/cheap viewers both count), and cites that seat-price losses (7) outnumber feature losses (3) and that those losses involved occasional/view-only users going to usage or free-viewer competitors. A recommendation to keep per-seat pricing because losses are feature-driven does not count. Mentioning feature gaps (RLS, audit log export, embedding) as a secondary fix is fine.

mistakes_that_matter: Reporting Tallowbeam as per-seat ($25 or $40 per seat), missing its move to usage pricing.
Saying Sorrelgate still has a free Community tier.
Comparing Brisklane's $468 per year or Obsidra's annual-billed $180 against monthly-billed prices without normalizing.
Saying Kettleridge moved its core product to usage pricing.
Miscounting loss reasons, especially counting Quarrydown as a seat-price loss or counting no-decision and won deals as losses.
Recommending Ferrowind keep per-seat pricing on the grounds that losses are mainly about missing features.
Inventing competitor prices, deals or quotes not present in the files.
